expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate relied heavily on interviewer nudges to locate and diagnose the bug, but once pointed at the sweep's released-quantity logic, they correctly identified the original-vs-remaining count mechanism, made a targeted fix, and confirmed the suite went green. Self-directed clarification and post-fix reflection were largely absent.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate did not read the failing test or question the expected behavior until explicitly told to at +20s. Even then, at +35s they simply reported the diff numbers rather than asking any clarifying question about whether partially-shipped holds should only return unshipped units. All resolution of ambiguity was interviewer-driven rather than self-initiated.

At +65s the candidate named the exact mechanism — releasing the original count instead of the remaining count — which matches the actual root cause closely. However this insight came directly after a pointed nudge at +50s telling them to look at what quantity the sweep releases, so it cannot be credited as self-directed hypothesis formation.

The candidate verbalized their read of the failure diff at +35s and their mechanism hypothesis at +65s, giving the interviewer visibility into their reasoning at those two points. But there is no narration during the actual edit, save, or test-run phases (+95s to +140s), leaving the execution stretch opaque.

The edit and save at +95s and +105s directly reflect the stated mechanism (original vs. remaining count), and the change was scoped tightly to sweep.ts without any scattered or contradictory edits. The subsequent passing test run at +140s confirms the implementation matched the diagnosis.

The candidate re-ran the full test suite after the fix and observed a PASS at +140s before ending the session, meeting the baseline bar of confirming before declaring done. There is no evidence, however, of checking that full-release (non-partial) holds still behave correctly or any deeper edge-case reasoning beyond the single green run.

After the tests passed, the candidate simply ended the session at +150s without articulating why the remaining-count fix resolves the phantom-stock issue or connecting the result back to the mechanism named earlier. The mechanism statement at +65s came before the fix, not as a post-hoc explanation of why it worked.
